ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, points $A$, $B$, and $C$ are three points on the circle $\odot O$, with $AC=BC$. Point $M$ is another point on $\odot O$, and $CE$ is perpendicular to $AM$, with the foot of the perpendicular being point $E$. Given that $AE=2\sqrt{3}$, $BM=\sqrt{3}$, and $CM=\sqrt{7}$, what is the length of arc $\overset{\frown}{CM}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let's cut $AG=BM$ on $AE$, and connect $CG$,\\
since $AC=BC$ and $\angle A=\angle B$,\\
thus $\triangle ACG \cong \triangle BCM$ (SAS),\\
hence $CG=CM=\sqrt{7}$,\\
since $AE=2\sqrt{3}$ and $AG=BM=\sqrt{3}$,\\
thus $GE=\sqrt{3}$,\\
since $CE\perp AM$,\\
thus $CE = \sqrt{CG^{2} - GE^{2}} = \sqrt{(\sqrt{7})^2 - (\sqrt{3})^2} = 2$,\\
thus $\tan\angle A = \frac{CE}{AE} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$,\\
thus $\angle A = 30^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle COM = 60^\circ$,\\
connect $OM$ and $CO$,\\
since $OC=OM$,\\
thus $\triangle COM$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
thus $OC=\sqrt{7}$,\\
thus the length of $\overset{\frown}{CM} = \frac{60\pi \times \sqrt{7}}{180} = \boxed{\frac{\sqrt{7}}{3}\pi}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a circle with center O. Points A, B, C, and M lie on the circle; C is near the top, A is on the left, B is lower right, and M is upper right. Segments AC, BC, CM, BM, and AM are drawn. Point E lies on AM, and CE is drawn perpendicular to AM with a right-angle mark at E. Reasoning: Choose point G on AE such that AG = BM = √3. Since AE = 2√3, we get GE = AE − AG = √3. Connect CG. Because G lies on AM, angle CAG equals angle CAM. The inscribed angles angle CAM and angle CBM subtend the same arc CM, so angle CAG = angle CBM. Also AC = BC and AG = BM, hence triangles ACG and BCM are congruent by SAS. Therefore CG = CM = √7. Since CE is perpendicular to AM and G,E lie on AM, triangle CGE is right at E. Thus CE = √(CG^2 − GE^2) = √(7 − 3) = 2. In right triangle ACE, tan(angle CAM) = CE/AE = 2/(2√3) = 1/√3, so angle CAM = 30°. By the inscribed angle theorem, the central angle angle COM is 60°, i.e. π/3 radians. The chord CM = √7 subtends 60°, so CM = 2R sin 30° = R, hence the circle radius R = √7. Therefore the length of arc CM is R·π/3 = √7π/3.
